record.paper_title: Open problems in queueing theory inspired by datacenter computing
record.original_question: For the M/M/k queue with setup times, where idle servers shut down and must incur setup delay before serving jobs again, can one derive a simple approximation as a function of k that captures how the response-time effect of setup diminishes in larger systems?

evidence.quote: It would be very nice to have a simple approximation for the M/M/k/setup as a function of k.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the M/M/k queueing system with server setup times, defined as follows. Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process of rate λ to a system with k identical servers, each of which serves jobs at exponential rate μ; let ρ = λ/(kμ) < 1 denote the load. Each server can be in one of three states: BUSY (currently serving a job), OFF, or SETUP. A server in the OFF state cannot serve jobs; when a job needs a server and an OFF server is available, that server enters the SETUP state, during which it incurs an Exp(α) setup delay before it can begin serving. Whenever a server completes a job and no jobs are waiting, it immediately transitions to OFF. Jobs waiting in a FCFS queue are assigned to servers as soon as any server becomes BUSY-ready.

Let E[T(k)] denote the mean response time (sojourn time) of a job in this system, and let E[T_{M/M/k}] denote the corresponding mean response time in the standard M/M/k system (no setup) with the same λ, μ, k.

Problem: Derive a simple closed-form approximation, as an explicit function of k (and of the other parameters λ, μ, α, ρ), for E[T(k)] in the M/M/k/Setup system that accurately captures how the additional response-time penalty E[T(k)] − E[T_{M/M/k}] due to setup behaves and diminishes as k grows large.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Williams, Harchol-Balter and collaborators, 2023–2024 PhD thesis and SIGMETRICS/ACM publications, plus a 2025 arXiv preprint) has produced closed-form multiplicatively-tight lower and upper bounds and a highly accurate approximation for mean waiting time in many-server systems with setup times (mainly deterministic setup, and with offered load R = kρ assumed reasonably large). For the exponential-setup M/M/k/Setup case, earlier closed-form approximations by Gandhi–Harchol-Balter exist. Thus the question has been substantially addressed for large k, though a single canonical "simple approximation as a function of k" for the general M/M/k/Setup remains an active topic rather than a fully closed problem.

status_evidence.title: The M/M/k with Deterministic Setup Times
status_evidence.snippet: Multiplicatively-tight lower and upper bounds on average waiting time in M/M/k/Setup; first closed-form bounds in any many-server system with setup times, used to derive a highly-accurate approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Closed-form bounds and an accurate approximation for M/M/k/Setup waiting time exist for large k.

status_evidence.title: Setup Times in Multiserver Systems (PhD thesis, CMU-CS-24-104)
status_evidence.snippet: Thesis devoted to approximations and bounds for multiserver queues with setup times.
status_evidence.claim: Substantial recent progress on simple approximations for M/M/k/Setup as a function of k.

status_evidence.title: M/G/k with Exponential Setup (Gandhi, Harchol-Balter)
status_evidence.snippet: Analytical approximations for M/G/k and M/M/k with exponential setup.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier closed-form approximations for the exponential-setup case were developed.

status_evidence.title: An Upper Bound on the M/M/k Queue With Deterministic Setup Times
status_evidence.snippet: Closed-form upper bound on the M/M/k queue with deterministic setup times.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2025 work refines simple bounds/approximations as a function of k.
